statements.statement: Owner: Executive director, until the board names an owner
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call named no owner, so the template default applies.

statements.statement: Next review: in 12 months
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call gave no review date, so the 12-month default applies.

statements.statement: We want AI to take routine writing off our plate. We must protect SNAP applicants, donors and volunteers, and keep a real person for anyone who needs help.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches the staff hope (newsletters, posts), Marcus's leak worry, and the wish for a person on the SNAP line.

statements.statement: Staff, volunteers, contractors and board members.
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: It says volunteers are covered while volunteer AI use is an open question; say who is covered but leave volunteer use to the board, or word it neutrally.

statements.statement: Gemini (in Google Workspace): Drafting and editing only; no protected information.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said people will use Gemini because it comes with Workspace; no protected information is the cautious limit.

statements.statement: New tools: Ken (IT) approves new tools, plugins, AI agents and AI features in existing software, after checking data and vendor training.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said Ken approves tools; the checks are the template default.

statements.statement: Accounts: Use your work Google account and turn off vendor training on what you type.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default for accounts; the call was silent.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Everyone, now: Staff may use Gemini in a work account for work with no information about a real person.
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Whether volunteers may use AI is an open question, but the policy covers them; 'staff' is fine here, yet it leaves volunteers unaddressed in the policy while the guidance says everyone; clarify that volunteer use awaits the board.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Draft newsletters and social posts.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Staff hope AI handles newsletters and social posts; works in Gemini.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Write general volunteer thank-yous; add names yourself afterward.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Volunteer thank-yous were named as a hope; names are added by hand to avoid personal data in the tool.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Draft grant boilerplate about our work.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Grant boilerplate was named as a hoped-for use.

statements.statement: SNAP or donor information in any AI tool — Marcus (CEO)
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: SNAP data is listed as never going into a tool and no tool is approved for it, so it cannot also be approvable; Marcus said he signs off on anything touching SNAP or donor data, so move SNAP out to off limits or limit this to donor data.

statements.statement: Reports to funders or Feeding America — Your manager
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call called it risky but named no approver, so the manager default applies.

statements.statement: Recall notices or allergen information — Your manager
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call flagged this as harmful but named no approver; manager default.

statements.statement: Anything using a corporate partner's logo or brand — Your manager
statements.label: default
statements.reason: A partner AI clause covers brand use; no approver named, so manager default.

statements.statement: Information that never goes in: SNAP applicants' Social Security numbers, income, household members and immigration documents (state human services agreement); donor names and giving records in Salesforce; volunteer names, phone numbers, emergency contacts and court-ordered case details; mobile pantry sign-up names and zip codes; passwords and logins.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: All types and the state agreement come from the call; passwords are always listed.

statements.statement: No AI answers SNAP eligibility questions. A person answers the SNAP line.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said he would never want a chatbot answering eligibility questions and a person answers the SNAP line.

statements.statement: No AI images of hungry people. Our photos are real, with consent forms.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said this directly.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: Whoever sends AI-assisted work owns it. Check facts, names, numbers and tone first.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default; the call named no reviewer.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: Pounds and people served come from the inventory system, never an AI draft.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said those numbers come from the inventory system, not a draft.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: Check recall and allergen details against the original notice.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Follows from Tasha's concern about a wrongly summarized recall.

statements.statement: AI never decides who gets help, benefits or a volunteer role. Trained people decide.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Follows from the SNAP harm concerns and trained, certified outreach staff; the volunteer role part is a cautious extension of the template.

statements.statement: We follow the AI clause in our corporate partner's agreement.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said one partner's agreement has an AI clause.

statements.statement: If a funder or partner asks about our AI use, we answer honestly.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call said partners will ask but set no rule; this is a cautious general default.

statements.statement: Tell your manager and Ken the same day. Reporting a mistake is expected, never punished.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Tasha gave the who and same-day timing; no-punishment is the template default.

statements.statement: The executive director owns this policy until the board names someone; Ken approves tools.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Owner default, and Ken approving tools is from the call.

statements.statement: The board's executive committee approves changes. We review it in 12 months.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Marcus said the executive committee should approve the policy; review is the default.

statements.statement: Who should own this policy day to day?
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: The owner is already settled as the executive director by default in the header and ownership section; this duplicates a decision, so drop it or leave the owner open in the header.

statements.statement: Do we approve or stop staff's personal ChatGPT and Claude use, and will we pay for any AI accounts next year?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Unsettled on the call: personal ChatGPT and Claude use and next year's budget.

statements.statement: Should AI reminder texts in the volunteer scheduling software stay on, and do we tell people when AI helped write what they get?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Tasha said no label needed but nobody settled it; the feature came with an update.

statements.statement: May volunteers, such as group leaders writing shift notes, use AI?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Tasha asked this and it was not settled.

missed: Marcus's sign-off on anything touching SNAP or donor data is not reflected cleanly as a rule for donor data alone.
Gemini (in Workspace) is not tied to a clear statement that it may not receive protected data such as donor names, which the 'Everyone, now' line only implies.
No-chatbot-answering-the-public rule is limited to SNAP; community wants a person to answer generally.
Pantry client and partner pantry data is not clarified as largely not held by Northgate.
Corporate partner's AI clause content is not described, so staff cannot tell what it requires.
